posts.title: Welcome to Talaria
posts.excerpt: Why we built a focused error-tracking stack for PHP and browser apps.
posts.body:
Talaria captures exceptions, messages, and session context so you can fix issues faster.

This harness blog is rendered client-side from a local JSON fixture — useful for testing the npm @newtalaria/browser SDK alongside Silverstripe.
posts.author: Talaria Team

posts.title: PHP SDK quickstart
posts.excerpt: Wire Monolog and TalariaClient into a Silverstripe project in minutes.
posts.body:
Install newtalaria/logging, set TALARIA_DSN and TALARIA_API_KEY, then flush after critical request paths.

Prefer the Injector client over calling Talaria::init repeatedly in controllers.
posts.author: Ada Lovelace

posts.title: Browser SDK with Vite
posts.excerpt: Bundle @newtalaria/browser from npm instead of relying on the CDN inject.
posts.body:
For app-owned frontends, install @newtalaria/browser, call Talaria.init once with DSN and API key, then route structured logs through a thin logger facade.

Keep replaysSessionSampleRate low in production and prefer error clips.
posts.author: Grace Hopper

posts.title: Tags that actually help
posts.excerpt: entity, operation, and source tags make dashboard filters useful.
posts.body:
Use stable tags like source=talaria_ss_test and entity=BlogDetailPage so harness traffic is easy to isolate.

Avoid high-cardinality values (user ids, UUIDs) as tag keys — put those in extra or userId.
posts.author: Talaria Team

posts.title: Instrumenting a checkout workflow
posts.excerpt: Milestone messages and handled payment failures with flush at the end.
posts.body:
Bootstrap tags and user context at the start of the action, emit a message per step, and capture handled exceptions without losing the stack.

Always flush() before redirecting so the batch leaves the process.
posts.author: Kathleen Booth
